finding: The round-12 repair closed only half the region defect, and the artifact documents the half that was not closed. `spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md` states "Entries live under the heading below and nowhere else — the check reads only that section, so a draft or superseded list elsewhere in this file is not part of the guard set." The check does not read only that section: `check_guard_doc` takes `body = text[heading.end():]`, i.e. everything from the `## Guard tests` heading to EOF, with no bound at the next heading. Entries before the heading are excluded (the round-12 fix); entries after the guard section, in any later heading, still count as listed. Verified by mutation against the real check and the real 100-entry derivation: a document whose `## Guard tests` section holds 90 of the 100 derived entries, with the remaining 10 under a following `## Excluded from the sweep` heading, produces zero failures and zero PENDING — exit 0, acceptance reached. This falsifies §7.1's stated implication that exit 0 with no `PENDING` line is "reachable only once the list is written, matches the derivation as a set": the list the §7 sweep is capped at holds 90, the derivation holds 100, and the observer reports agreement. The failure mode is invited rather than hypothetical — the doc's own sentence tells the first-task author that entries parked outside the guard section are not part of the guard set, so an author who follows the documentation and separates triage or exclusions into a second section produces a green false state, over an artifact produced after review closes that no reviewer will ever see.

resolved.evidence: The list region is bounded on both sides: entries count under the Guard tests heading and above the next one. Mutation-tested with both counter-examples -- 80 hidden above the heading and 10 under a following heading now fail, while the full correct list passes with no PENDING.

suggestion: Bound the region at the next heading so the check implements the rule already documented: after locating the heading, cut `body` at the next `^## ` match (`nxt = re.search(r"^## ", body, re.M); body = body[:nxt.start()] if nxt else body`), and record beside it that the extent is the section, not the file tail. The alternative repair — deleting the doc's "and nowhere else / reads only that section" sentence and stating the true to-EOF rule — leaves the same escape open in a differently-worded form, because §7.1 still calls the artifact "the list" the sweep is capped at while the check would accept entries the document files under any other heading.

finding: Round 12 idx 0 was recorded fixed with "The guard document now has a Guard tests heading and the check reads entries from that section only, so a draft or commented-out list elsewhere in the file is not part of the guard set. Mutation-tested: 20 entries under the heading with 80 in a comment above now fails." Verified against the current script rather than the evidence line: the region is bounded on one side only. check-measured-claims.py:180 is `body = text[heading.end():]` — it runs to end of file, with no section terminator — while the comment above it (:73-75) and spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md:31-32 both assert section scoping ("Entries count only under this heading"; "the check reads only that section, so a draft or superseded list elsewhere in this file is not part of the guard set"). The unscoped direction is the one the document's layout makes natural: `## Guard tests` is the LAST line of the file (line 34), so every line the first task writes lands after it. Mutation-tested in a clone of c512809, both directions of the original finding: (a) 20 entries under `## Guard tests` with the other 80 in an HTML comment ABOVE the heading -> exit 1, the recorded repair holds; (b) the same 20 entries under `## Guard tests` followed by a section `## Deferred (not swept this release)` holding the other 80 -> exit 0, no PENDING. Case (b) is round 12's counter-example with the two blocks swapped, and §7.1 invites exactly that arrangement — it hands the first task triage ordering over "of the order of a hundred functions" (line 185-186), and an in-scope / deferred split is the obvious way to record it. §7.1:200, "The sweep is capped at that list plus any test a removal decision depends on", then has the same two readings over the same green artifact that round 12 recorded as closed: a later sweep task reading the document sees a cap of 20, the check certifies 100, and nothing distinguishes them. Not the wider defect the parent finding had — the set equality still forces the entries in aggregate to equal the derivation exactly, so the sweep set cannot be wrong, only its declared extent.
